content: The objective of the CORONA trial was to investigate the effects of administering 10 mg of rosuvastatin daily in patients diagnosed with congestive heart failure. The study, known as the Controlled Rosuvastatin Multinational Trial in Heart Failure (CORONA), was designed as a double-blinded, randomized, placebo-controlled trial. A total of 5,011 patients with congestive heart failure classified as New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class II, III, or IV ischemic systolic heart failure were enrolled. These participants were randomly assigned to receive either 10 mg of rosuvastatin daily or a placebo. The primary endpoint of the study was defined as death from cardiovascular causes, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), or non-fatal stroke. The results demonstrated that rosuvastatin, compared to placebo, effectively reduced serum low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol levels while increasing high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol and triglyceride levels. However, there was no statistically significant reduction in mortality rates due to cardiovascular causes, coronary events, or all-cause mortality.
